faqs.question: Is the 5 Day Marangu Route recommended?
faqs.answer: It is possible for fit travelers with limited time, but it is not our first choice for acclimatization.

faqs.question: Why choose 6 Day Marangu instead?
faqs.answer: The 6 day route adds an acclimatization day at Horombo before moving to Kibo Hut.

faqs.question: Does Marangu use tents?
faqs.answer: No. Marangu uses shared mountain huts.

faqs.question: Can I join a group?

faqs.question: Is summit night difficult?
faqs.answer: Yes. It begins around midnight and reaches high altitude before the long descent to Horombo.

faqs.question: Can I add a safari?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many travelers add a Serengeti safari or Zanzibar after this shorter climb.

faqs.question: How are your Kilimanjaro guides prepared for safety?
faqs.answer: Our climbs are led by licensed and well trained Kilimanjaro guides. They are trained to recognize altitude related warning signs, complete regular health checks, manage the walking pace and respond when a climber needs to stop or descend.

faqs.question: How do you monitor climbers on the mountain?
faqs.answer: Guides check how you feel and use a pulse oximeter to monitor pulse and blood oxygen readings. They consider the readings together with your symptoms and how your condition changes over time.

faqs.question: When is emergency oxygen used?
faqs.answer: Emergency oxygen is carried for stabilization during descent or evacuation when health checks and established safety procedures show that it is needed. It is not used to help a climber continue towards the summit.

faqs.question: What happens if health checks show that continuing could be unsafe?
faqs.answer: Your guide will explain the concern, provide support and follow established mountain safety procedures. When required, the team coordinates with the national park rescue service.

faqs.question: What travel insurance is required?
faqs.answer: Your policy should cover trekking up to 6,000 metres, medical treatment, evacuation and repatriation. Helicopter support depends on weather, landing conditions and the terms of your insurance.

faqs.question: Is 6 Day Marangu better than 5 Day Marangu?
faqs.answer: For most travelers, yes. The extra day at Horombo gives your body more time to adjust before moving to Kibo.

faqs.question: Is Marangu the only hut route?
faqs.answer: Yes. Marangu is the main Kilimanjaro route that uses shared mountain huts rather than tents.

faqs.question: Are the huts private?
faqs.answer: No. The huts are shared and private rooms are not normally available on the mountain.

faqs.question: Can beginners choose this route?
faqs.answer: Yes, with proper training and equipment. The direct trail and summit night still require strong preparation.

faqs.question: Can I join a group?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose one of the guaranteed joining dates published on this page.

faqs.question: What deposit is required?
faqs.answer: A 10 percent deposit secures your booking after the date and route are confirmed.

faqs.question: How are your Kilimanjaro guides prepared for safety?
faqs.answer: Our climbs are led by licensed and well trained Kilimanjaro guides. They are trained to recognize altitude related warning signs, complete regular health checks, manage the walking pace and respond when a climber needs to stop or descend.

faqs.question: How do you monitor climbers on the mountain?
faqs.answer: Guides check how you feel and use a pulse oximeter to monitor pulse and blood oxygen readings. They consider the readings together with your symptoms and how your condition changes over time.

faqs.question: When is emergency oxygen used?
faqs.answer: Emergency oxygen is carried for stabilization during descent or evacuation when health checks and established safety procedures show that it is needed. It is not used to help a climber continue towards the summit.

faqs.question: What happens if health checks show that continuing could be unsafe?
faqs.answer: Your guide will explain the concern, provide support and follow established mountain safety procedures. When required, the team coordinates with the national park rescue service.

faqs.question: What travel insurance is required?
faqs.answer: Your policy should cover trekking up to 6,000 metres, medical treatment, evacuation and repatriation. Helicopter support depends on weather, landing conditions and the terms of your insurance.

faqs.question: How are your Kilimanjaro guides prepared for safety?

faqs.question: Why choose 7 Day Rongai instead of 6 Day Rongai?
faqs.answer: The seven day route divides the early northern stages and gives a steadier schedule before Kibo Hut.

faqs.question: Is Rongai less crowded?
faqs.answer: It generally has fewer climbers than Machame and Marangu because it begins on the northern side.

faqs.question: Does Rongai use huts or tents?
faqs.answer: Rongai uses tents until the descent, when the route reaches Horombo Hut.

faqs.question: Is hotel accommodation included?

faqs.question: Can private groups choose their own date?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private departures are available on your preferred date, subject to guide and park arrangements.

faqs.question: How are your Kilimanjaro guides prepared for safety?
faqs.answer: Our climbs are led by licensed and well trained Kilimanjaro guides. They are trained to recognize altitude related warning signs, complete regular health checks, manage the walking pace and respond when a climber needs to stop or descend.

faqs.question: How do you monitor climbers on the mountain?
faqs.answer: Guides check how you feel and use a pulse oximeter to monitor pulse and blood oxygen readings. They consider the readings together with your symptoms and how your condition changes over time.

faqs.question: When is emergency oxygen used?
faqs.answer: Emergency oxygen is carried for stabilization during descent or evacuation when health checks and established safety procedures show that it is needed. It is not used to help a climber continue towards the summit.

faqs.question: What happens if health checks show that continuing could be unsafe?
faqs.answer: Your guide will explain the concern, provide support and follow established mountain safety procedures. When required, the team coordinates with the national park rescue service.

faqs.question: What travel insurance is required?
faqs.answer: Your policy should cover trekking up to 6,000 metres, medical treatment, evacuation and repatriation. Helicopter support depends on weather, landing conditions and the terms of your insurance.

faqs.question: When is emergency oxygen used?

faqs.question: What happens if health checks show that continuing could be unsafe?
